is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates pirimiphos-methyl resistance in the major malaria vectors Anopheles gambiae and A. coluzzii (Page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports on the Ace-1 G280S (also known as G119S) SNP and Ace-1 copy number variation (CNV) or duplication (Page 3, Results).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 (Page 7) provides genotype frequencies (wt / wt+280S / 280S) and sample sizes (n) for nine West African populations.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, and Togo (Page 7, Table 1; Page 20, Methods). It also uses data from the Ag1000G project covering multiple African countries (Page 4, Fig 1).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research article reporting new field collections, bioassays, and genomic analyses (Page 1).

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is reported for specific sites including Tiassalé, Aboisso (Côte d'Ivoire), Korle-Bu, Madina, Weija, Obuasi (Ghana), and Baguida (Togo) (Page 7, Table 1; Page 20, Methods).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The new field collections were conducted between May and September 2012 (Page 19, Methods).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study utilizes whole-genome sequencing data from the Anopheles gambiae 1000 Genomes project (Phase 2 AR1), which is a publicly available and previously published dataset (Page 1, Data Availability; Page 19, Methods). However, it also presents new genotype-phenotype data for 1080 specimens collected specifically for this study.

supplement.evidence: Extractable genotype counts and frequencies for the primary association analysis are provided in Table 1 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This study investigates the genetic basis of pirimiphos-methyl resistance in West African Anopheles gambiae and An. coluzzii. It identifies a complex resistance haplotype involving both the Ace-1 G280S (G119S) mutation and Ace-1 gene duplications (CNV). The study combines whole-genome data from the Ag1000G project with new field collections and bioassays from Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, and Togo (n=1080), demonstrating that the combination of SNP and CNV is a strong predictor of resistance and has spread via introgression between species.
